finding: Early drafts risked treating the Good-Chalmers recursive feedback loop as an inevitability rather than a conditional hypothesis with unverified parameter thresholds.
action_taken: Disaggregated intelligence explosion into a 3-tier taxonomy (AI-assisted R&D vs RSI vs Explosive Takeoff), added 16 structural friction factors, and established unweighted parameter regimes.

finding: Treating capability asymmetry as a single scalar index or IQ equivalent is scientifically indefensible and conflates linguistic mastery with physical competence.
action_taken: Explicitly refuted scalar g-factor models, cited Chollet (2019) and Brooks (2017), and formulated a candidate 14-dimensional Asymmetry Profile vector across discrete cognitive and physical faculties.

finding: Safety evaluation benchmarks showing in-context scheming (Meinke et al.) or alignment faking (Greenblatt et al.) are heavily prompt-steered and single-lab; labeling them as established scientific facts (Class A) would violate Rule S4.
action_taken: Strictly classified model-organism scheming evaluations as Class B, tagged lab self-reports in reviewer flags, and added Sclar et al. (2024) prompt sensitivity findings (up to 76 pt swing) as an essential methodological constraint.

finding: Takeoff literature often ignores internal organizational frictions and general equilibrium constraints, assuming an AI can expand without internal coordination loss.
action_taken: Incorporated Joshua Gans (2017/2018) principal-agent contracting model of AGI self-regulation, derived Baumol's cost disease under CES production (Aghion et al. 2019), and cited Nordhaus (2021) 7 econometric singularity rejections.

finding: Corrigibility failures in tool-using agents (Palisade 2025, CMU ROGUE 2026) could be misinterpreted as emergent self-preservation drives rather than myopic task-completion pressure.
action_taken: Clarified in the empirical review that current agentic shutdown resistance is driven by subtask decomposition loops treating termination as an error to be retried, not conscious self-preservation.

finding: Standard discussions conflate operational control (holding a kill-switch) with meaningful human agency, leading to false complacency about human-in-the-loop safeguards.
action_taken: Disaggregated vocabulary into 5 distinct constructs (Control, Understanding, Agency, Participation, Sovereignty), mapped the 'Control without Agency' failure mode (rubber-stamping), and evaluated real-world precedents (Robodebt, Flash Crash).

finding: Early scenario profile drafts contained speculative risk claims supported primarily by informal blog posts and essays (Tier 5), risking violation of Rule S1 and source tier hierarchy.
action_taken: Enforced peer-reviewed academic foundations (Tier 1 & 2) for all core scenario premises, grounded thought experiments in formal MDP theorems (Turner et al.) or macroeconomic growth models, and explicitly marked speculative premises as Class E/F.

finding: Skeptics and concerned researchers frequently talk past each other by using contradictory definitions of 'intelligence' and 'alignment', creating artificial impasses.
action_taken: Constructed the 8-crux Disagreement Register (disagreements.csv), isolating definitional equivocation (e.g. optimization power vs skill-acquisition efficiency) from genuine empirical disputes (e.g. substitution elasticity sigma).
